patch_description: The current ansatz uses 5 distinct parameters (ry_a, ry_b, rz_a, rz_b, ry_c) and shows a large train/validation gap (0.81 vs 0.63, gap=0.20), indicating overfitting/high capacity relative to the tiny training set. Since parameter economy is rewarded at every count and reducing the generalization gap is explicitly valued, I merge the two alternating-qubit rotation layers (ry_a/ry_b and rz_a/rz_b) into single shared parameters each (ry_a, rz_a). This cuts the parameter count from 5 to 3 distinct trainable parameters while keeping the same gate structure/depth (same expressive entangling pattern), which should reduce overfitting, tighten the generalization gap, and improve parameter efficiency — all while preserving the diverse two-directional CNOT ring entangling structure that worked reasonably well.
